principle: One writer per overlapping path or ref. Generated artifacts are serialized behind their single generator. Overlap between two active owners is a collision that must be serialized before either proceeds.

refs.note: Integration through the normal reviewable PR process; no direct push.
Exact fast-forward to hosted-verified dev SHA; non-release.
Isolated agent continuation branches; reversible local work.
Isolated continuation branches for seats recovered after a lost session; reversible local work, never pushed directly to dev or main.

paths.note: Machine-readable governance contracts; one documentation maker per path.
Contract schemas evolve with contracts under the same lane.
Generated views only; never hand-edited. Written solely by opsctl render behind the governance lane.
One current work capsule per ticket; the ticket's writer lease owns it.
Append-only event chain per ticket; written behind the same per-ticket lane as the capsule it records.
Writer leases are issued and revoked by the deputy; every lease records issuer it-manager-iii.
Reconstruction bundle is read-only authority for installation; changes are protected.
Game source. Implementation only; sequencing and gating belong to it-manager-iii and are not path writes.
Produced art and asset packages staged by the authoring seat.
Structured game content; the data contract owner withholds unsafe shapes.
Fixtures and red plants belong to the independent verifier, not to the seat under test.
Art contracts and motif records authored alongside the assets they describe.
Census, classification and sequencing records; distinct from the machine-readable contracts.
Intake and routing records surfaced to design.
Repo tooling and support scripts. Restores the ability to work; product behaviour changes belong to maker.

generated_serialization.rule: A generated view is regenerated from validated JSON and never edited by hand. opsctl render is the sole writer; opsctl render --check proves the committed view matches its sources with no drift.

collision_rule: Two active owners whose path globs overlap, or two writers on the same ref, are a collision. The affected transition fails closed and the owning role serializes the lane before either proceeds; unrelated reversible work continues.
